title_en: World Bank Irrigation Development Project (with Additional Financing)
implementers: Government of Armenia irrigation-sector project implementation unit
budget_original: IDA credit US$24.86 million at approval (World Bank data) plus Additional Financing of US$5.0 million (2008); actual total project cost US$33.85 million (ICR Annex 1).
summary_en: The project rehabilitated critical irrigation structures, converted three pump-fed irrigation schemes to gravity supply and helped set up Water User Associations and water-supply agencies under participatory irrigation management. The Additional Financing (2008) scaled up WUA support and rehabilitation of additional tertiary systems and extended closing to March 2009.
activities_en: Rehabilitation of critical irrigation structures: Araks river intake of the Armavir scheme, Hoktemberyan main conveyance canal, Myasnikyan secondary canal, and 69 emergency structures in the Shirak, Armavir, Talin, Arzni-Shamiram, Vayots Dzor and Vorotan irrigation systems
Conversion from pumping to gravity irrigation in the Yeghegnadzor, Aygedzor and Ayrum schemes
Institutional development: establishment of Water User Associations (18 WUAs on 47,355 ha in 2003, 36 more on 86,035 ha in 2004) and consolidation of the Water Supply Agency
Water-management accounting software introduced in 33 WUAs
results_en: Araks intake capacity raised from 27 to 53 m3/s (completed April 2004)
Actually irrigated area rose from 113,400 ha (2004) to 128,600 ha (2008)
Irrigation fee collection rose by about 1,232 million AMD (55.7 percent) between 2004 and 2008
Electricity use fell from 119.2 to 110.3 million kWh (2004 to 2008)

locations.evidence: ICR: WUAs were established nationwide (18 WUAs in 2003 and 36 in 2004) and the Water Supply Agency was restructured into four regional branches.
ICR Annex 2: capacity expansion of the Armavir irrigation scheme (Araks river intake, Hoktemberyan main canal, Myasnikyan secondary canal).

title_en: World Bank Irrigation Dam Safety Projects (Dam Safety Project and Second Irrigation Dam Safety Project)
implementers: Government of Armenia dam-safety project implementation unit
national_partners: State Committee on Water Systems / Water Resources Management Agency
budget_original: Dam Safety Project: actual cost US$32.61 million (appraisal US$30.30 million); Second Irrigation Dam Safety Project: actual cost US$8.40 million (appraisal US$7.50 million), per the two ICRs. World Bank credit amounts: US$26.6 million and US$6.75 million.
summary_en: Two linked World Bank projects reduced the risk of failure at Armenia's most dangerous irrigation dams. The first rehabilitated the 20 highest-risk dams (after dam failures in 1974, 1979 and 1994) and the second financed safety works at a further group of dams, with dam surveillance, emergency plans and institutional reform.
activities_en: Rehabilitation works at 20 priority dams (e.g. Arpilich, Aygedzor, Halavar, Azat, Vardakar, Tavshut, Sovetashen, David-Bek, Sevaberd, Aparan, Karnut, Mantash, Sarnakhbjur, Hakhum, Tavush, Gegardalich, Gegharkunik-2, Kakavadzor-2, Upper Bazmaberd, Herher)
First project ended with 27 dams rehabilitated (the 20 planned plus seven more); the second project targeted 47 further dams and completed 44; Kaps dam rehabilitation was handed to MCC
Emergency preparedness plans, operation and maintenance plans and monitoring equipment per dam
Legal framework (Water Code, law on dam safety) and a dam-safety regulatory function
results_en: 44 dams rehabilitated under the second project (94 percent of target)
Risk-reduction target for the 20 original dams reached in 2004

settlements: Zangakatun dam (Ararat marz, mentioned in the ICR)
locations.evidence: ICR (Dam Safety Project): 'The project was largely national in scope as the 20 dams to be rehabilitated were located in nine out of the 10 Marzes (provinces)'; the second project targeted 47 further dams of the 87 dams in the national inventory.

title_en: MCC / Millennium Challenge Account-Armenia Irrigated Agriculture Project (Infrastructure Activity and Water-to-Market Activity)
implementers: Irrigation PIU under the State Water Committee (until 2008)
national_partners: State Committee of Water Economy / Water Supply Agencies
budget_original: Original compact project amount US$145.67 million (Infrastructure US$113.2 million, Water-to-Market US$32.4 million); total disbursed US$153.7 million (MCC Closed Compact Report).
summary_en: The largest irrigation refurbishment in Armenia's history under the MCC Compact. The Infrastructure Activity rehabilitated main canals, pumping stations, gravity systems, tertiary canals and drainage in the Ararat Valley and other regions; the Water-to-Market Activity trained farmers, provided credit and strengthened WUAs and water supply agencies.
activities_en: Six main canals rehabilitated (41.8 km lined, over 260 structures)
17 irrigation pumping stations rehabilitated; five pump-to-gravity conversions (almost 50 km of canals)
Tertiary canals rehabilitated in more than 100 communities (232.8 km, 15 percent community co-financing)
470 km of drainage canals cleaned in the Ararat and Armavir regions
Support to 44 WUAs and three water supply agencies (management improvement plans, 180 computers with GIS software); farmer training and rural credit (US$12.7 million, 1,008 borrowers)
results_en: Infrastructure activity ERR 24.4 percent at closure; Mathematica 2016 evaluation found improved water timeliness near tertiary canals but no evidence of higher irrigated area or household income
Water-to-Market: farmer training did not measurably change on-farm water management (2013 evaluation)
